It IS still there, but you only get offered it if you go for the uninstall button, the device-admin lock, the monitoring switch, or try to escape a locked strict mode. string-array.name: mode_strict_rules

A rough model, not a medical measurement. It exists to make a pattern visible, nothing more.
Hold a low baseline and you climb. The belts are earned by TIME - not one good day, but weeks of them. A rough week drops you fast; climbing back is the long game. That\'s the point.

Every rule below adds points to a daily total, capped at 100. Higher is worse. Nothing here is hidden from you.
Each category is worth points at a full dose. A \"full dose\" is %1$d hours or more in a day. Below that it scales up on a curve, so the fourth hour costs you more than the first.
Example: 2 hours of %1$s is half the maximum dose, which on the curve is about %2$d%% of %3$d points ≈ %4$d points.
Time spent between %1$d:00 and 0%2$d:00 is multiplied by %3$s — you pay twice, once for the hit and once for the sleep. Use in the first %4$d minutes after waking is multiplied by %5$s.
Nothing below %1$d an hour. Full points at %2$d an hour or more.
%1$d points each time you unlock the phone and are inside a feed within %2$d seconds. No decision happened there.
Based on the MOST times you opened any single app within one hour. Nothing below %1$s opens; full points at %2$s.
Interactions per minute of screen time. Nothing below %1$d/min (that\'s reading). Full points at %2$d/min (that\'s thumbing a feed).

Time with the screen off — up to %1$d points back, with full credit at %2$d waking hours off the phone.\n\nThat is deliberately small. A calm evening does not undo a four-hour binge, and a score that pretended it did would be no use to you.

Being straight with you about the holes:

• We cannot tell when you woke up. Android gives us no alarm signal, so we treat your first unlock after a %1$d+ hour gap as "just woke up". Nap and it'll misfire.

• Screen-off credit doesn't know whether a podcast is playing. Seeing that needs a permission this app deliberately doesn't take.

Two moves do most of the work: a real break away from your device, then locking it down hard for the week after. Everything else supports those two.
Get the troublesome ones out of easy reach.
Keep your phone out of the bedroom
Alarm clock so it never comes to bed - tap for the how.
Be out of the house as much as possible
Spend the money if you have to - on anything that isn\'t addictive. Friends and social clubs most of all.
Not just the apps - the accounts. Remove the pull entirely.
A clean visual reset every time you unlock.
Change your app theme, if you can
Make the phone feel like a different, less familiar device.
Go on holiday - without your device
Step right out of the environment the habit lives in. The single biggest reset.
Completed. You can run it again any time.
Do the holiday first - it\'s what protects the fresh start.
Lock yourself out for 7 days straight, right after the holiday.
Super-strict lock for a week after
Do the holiday first - it\'s what makes the lock stick.
More ways to keep the phone out of your hands.
The goal is simple: never need to bring your phone into the bedroom. If the phone isn\'t there at night, the highest-risk moments mostly disappear.
The single most important purchase. It removes the only honest reason to have the phone by your bed.
Charge your phone in another room
Pick a spot - kitchen, hallway - and make it the permanent overnight home for the phone.
So you never reach for the phone just to check the time.
Don\'t bring your phone to bed or high-risk spots
The bedroom, the bathroom, anywhere you\'ve slipped before. Leave it charging in another room.
Change your state when an urge hits
A shower, a cold blast at the end of it, a quick workout, stepping outside, a tight bedtime and wake-up routine, even a game - anything that breaks the moment and shifts how you feel.
Make the habit harder to reach by accident. Before anything else:
Move anything that tends to lead you in off your home screen - bury it in a folder, or remove the shortcut.
Sign out of accounts so opening them isn\'t one tap.
Delete the apps you don\'t truly need. The friction is the point.
Add the rest to this app\'s block list so they\'re handled for you.
Go on holiday / break the routine
The habit is wired to a place and a rhythm. The fastest way to weaken it is to physically leave that environment for a while.
Aim for a proper break - ideally around two weeks.
Go without your phone if you can, or leave it locked down the whole time.
Fill the days with people, movement and daylight - not screens.
Come back to a home you\'ve already rearranged, and start the 7-day lock fresh.
Strict mode stays on for 7 days. You can\'t switch back to relaxed until it ends. It\'s most effective once you\'ve reset with the holiday - you\'re protecting fresh ground, not fighting uphill.
Put the phone in another room and do the one thing you were avoiding for ten minutes.
